title: An aligned dipole and tilted octupole have no stable corotation-circle sites at a tuned ratio below 38.6 degrees
abstract: We test how a tilt changes magnetic cancellation near corotation in a fixed-field model for complex periodic variables. An aligned dipole and tilted octupole have no stable sites on the exact equatorial corotation circle when B3/B1=(4/3)x squared/cos(beta), for tilt between zero and 38.581183 degrees. Two points with zero quadratic stiffness are unstable at fourth order. Close to this ratio, two opposite stable arcs return. Their angular fraction is linear in vertical field detuning, and their integrated positive stiffness is cubic. At the aligned cancellation ratio, a one-degree tilt gives a stable angular fraction of 0.000802 and a small-oscillation period of about 115 stellar rotations at the arc centre. Polynomial roots, direct angular integration and 240 field-line tests check the results. This extends an aligned-field cancellation result without requiring a null on the circle. It does not remove traps at other radii or latitudes, explain an observed CPV rate, or identify material. The model omits pressure, field deformation, supply and optical transfer. Original proofs, code, synthetic tables, provenance and a figure are included.

display.caption: Exact stable fractions on the corotation circle and their small-detuning and small-tilt limits. The dashed line marks the tuned field ratio. These are fixed-field calculations, not observations.
